original_question: Let G be an abelian-by-nilpotent ordered group. (i) Is G order-embeddable in a divisible ordered group? (ii) If G is also nilpotent-by-abelian, is G order-embeddable in a divisible ordered group?
target_in_paper: Section 3 (“Totally ordered groups”), Problem 3.32*: “Let G be an abelian-by-nilpotent ordered group. (i) Is G order-embeddable in a divisible ordered group? (ii) If G is also nilpotent-by-abelian, is G order-embeddable in a divisible ordered group?” ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0906.2621.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft is already extremely close to the paper’s official wording: it matches the exact class of groups (abelian-by-nilpotent ordered groups), the exact conclusion sought (order-embeddability into a divisible ordered group), and the paper’s second strengthened clause under the extra nilpotent-by-abelian hypothesis. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0906.2621.pdf))
missing_details: The paper places this in Section 3 on ordered groups, so “ordered group” here should be read as a group with a total order compatible with the group operation in the ordered-group sense used in that section, not merely a right-orderable or left-orderable group. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0906.2621.pdf))

To make the question fully stand-alone, unpack “abelian-by-nilpotent” as: there exists a normal abelian subgroup A of G such that G/A is nilpotent. The paper uses the term without redefinition in Problem 3.32*. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0906.2621.pdf))

Likewise unpack “nilpotent-by-abelian” as: there exists a normal nilpotent subgroup N of G such that G/N is abelian. The paper uses this as the extra hypothesis in part (ii). ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0906.2621.pdf))

Make “order-embeddable” explicit as the existence of an injective group homomorphism that preserves and reflects the given order; the nearby Problem 3.14 uses the synonymous phrase “the embedding an o-embedding” in the ordered setting. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0906.2621.pdf))

Spell out “divisible ordered group” as a divisible group carrying a compatible total order. Problem 3.32 asks about embeddings into such groups, and Problem 3.33 immediately continues with “minimal divisible completion” for ordered groups that admit such an embedding. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0906.2621.pdf))

State the universal quantifier explicitly: the question is whether every ordered group G with the stated normal-series hypotheses has such an embedding; the paper imposes no finiteness, generation, or rank assumptions. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0906.2621.pdf))
refined_question: Let G be a group equipped with a bi-invariant total order <. Assume that G is abelian-by-nilpotent, meaning that G has a normal abelian subgroup A with nilpotent quotient G/A. Must there exist a divisible group D equipped with a bi-invariant total order <_D and an injective group homomorphism f:G -> D such that, for all x,y in G, x<y if and only if f(x)<_D f(y)? If, in addition, G is nilpotent-by-abelian, meaning that G has a normal nilpotent subgroup N with abelian quotient G/N, does the same conclusion follow? ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0906.2621.pdf))
justification: The draft is targeting Problem 3.32* exactly, not the neighboring Problem 3.14 or Problem 3.20. Problem 3.32* in Section 3 states the two-part question almost verbatim on p. 17. Section 3 is the correct ambient setting because it is the paper’s section on ordered/orderable groups. The nearby comments show why the problem should not be broadened: the paper records a positive result for metabelian G and a negative result for arbitrary ordered groups, while Problem 3.14 records a related but stricter negative question about embedding nilpotent-by-abelian groups into divisible groups of the same general type. So the faithful rewrite should stay narrowly with the exact abelian-by-nilpotent hypothesis, together with the paper’s separate strengthened clause under the additional nilpotent-by-abelian assumption. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0906.2621.pdf))
